notes: This is Phase 5 local implementation evidence, not native Linux or release/tag acceptance.
All five optimized native Windows scenarios pass. The four transports use Metalink admission with a complete SHA-256 chunk manifest and 1000 active HTTP ranges.
Each transport completes 20000 measured calls and 1000 additional mutation-verification calls, with every ordinary operation p99 at most 50 ms.
All measured bursts stay at most 1000 calls/500 ms, with at least 250 ms cooldown, renewed barriers, and a 90-second scenario deadline.

Compilation and fuzzing finished before benchmarks. Compiler/build process names were checked before each scenario and sampled every five seconds; no compiler was observed during any accepted scenario.
Working-set values are sampled engine-process maxima and exclude the external origin/client fixtures; reservations enforce independent hard admission limits.
Stdio measurements use native OS pipes. The second stalled framed writer is a loopback socket; the separately stalled event consumer is WebSocket.
The administrative scenario uses 128-task operations and zero active ranges; total administrative completion time is separate from urgent/query latency.

The 296 source-file hashes identify the implementation commit. Later evidence/status documentation and two added session-v2 fuzz seeds do not change compiled Rust/build inputs. The complete seed inventory is recorded separately.
Fuzz counts are libFuzzer executions, including corpus initialization and repeated seeds across bursts; they are not counts of distinct generated inputs.
Three fuzz processes exceeded 500 ms and are retained as excluded attempts. Turning off per-function printing and reducing batches preserved ASan and coverage instrumentation.
Publication redacts workstation paths in command records. Measurements and original artifact hashes are unchanged; source commit IDs and source-file hashes refer to the pre-publication history.
